# test_intersection.py
import pytest

from <module_under_test> import intersection   # replace <module_under_test> with the actual name


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Happy-path tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "lst1, lst2, expected",
    [
        ([1, 2, 3], [2, 3, 4], [2, 3]),                 # simple case
        ([3, 2, 1, 2], [2, 3],        [3, 2]),          # order follows lst1
        ([1, 2, 2, 2, 3], [2],        [2]),             # duplicates in lst1
        ([2, 2, 3, 3],   [3, 3, 2],   [2, 3]),          # duplicates in both lists
        (["a", "b", "c"], ["c", "a"], ["a", "c"]),      # non-numeric items
        ([],             [1, 2, 3],   []),              # empty first list
        ([1, 2, 3],      [],          []),              # empty second list
        ([],             [],          []),              # both empty
    ],
)
def test_intersection_happy_cases(lst1, lst2, expected):
    assert intersection(lst1, lst2) == expected


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Edge-case / corner-case tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_preserves_first_occurrence_only():
    """
    Even if an element appears several times in lst1, it must be present only
    once in the result – at the position of its first appearance.
    """
    lst1 = [5, 1, 5, 2, 5, 3]
    lst2 = [5, 3]
    assert intersection(lst1, lst2) == [5, 3]


def test_mixed_data_types():
    lst1 = [1, "1", (1,)]
    lst2 = ["1", (1,), 1]
    assert intersection(lst1, lst2) == [1, "1", (1,)]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Error-handling tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_unhashable_items_in_lst2_raise_type_error():
    """
    lst2 is converted to a set; if it contains unhashable elements (e.g. list),
    Python raises TypeError.
    """
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        intersection([1, 2, 3], [[1], 2])   # inner list is unhashable


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad_arg, good_arg", [(1, [1, 2]), ([1, 2], 1)])
def test_non_iterable_arguments_raise_type_error(bad_arg, good_arg):
    """
    Passing a non-iterable instead of a list should raise TypeError because
    the function tries to iterate over it or convert it to a set.
    """
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        intersection(bad_arg, good_arg)
